## From Artificial Intelligence to Physical AI

Founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center (DLR), Agile Robots develops robotic systems that combine artificial intelligence, sensors and precision engineering.

Its products range from industrial robotic arms and dexterous hands to mobile and humanoid robots, supported by proprietary software and AI models. [...] The distinction between conventional automation and Physical AI is commercially significant. Traditional industrial robots generally perform predefined tasks in structured environments. AI-enabled systems aim to interpret changing conditions and adapt their behaviour accordingly.

That could open up more complex activities in manufacturing, logistics and electronics assembly, where tasks have historically depended on human dexterity and judgement. [...] The valuation reflects expectations about the commercial potential of Physical AI, but it reveals relatively little about the company’s underlying financial performance.

Agile Robots has not disclosed revenue, profitability or detailed financial terms in its funding announcement.

Without those figures, investors and industry observers cannot assess the valuation against sales, earnings or cash generation.

items.title: The Individual Investors Who Are Hot on Anthropic’s IPO But Cool on AI - WSJ
items.snippet: The mixed emotions Comez and other individual investors feel about Anthropic and...
items.raw_snippet:
The mixed emotions Comez and other individual investors feel about Anthropic and AI stands in stark relief to the euphoria that greeted the IPO of Elon Musk’s SpaceX five months ago. AI fever was at its peak, powering a blistering chip-stock rally that tripled or even quadrupled stocks including Sandisk and Intel. The S&P 500 had just logged one of its best two-month stretches in history. And there was the star power of Musk himself. Few would confuse Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s following or [...] He’s still joining the crowd waiting in line for what is expected to be one of the biggest initial public offerings ever. It is a necessary step, Comez said, to avoid being left behind as AI sets the pace for the stock market in the coming years. [...] Alex Comez is still a bit wary of the whole artificial intelligence thing. But when shares of Anthropic start trading later this month, he wants in.

Comez, a 29-year-old chemist in Fargo, N.D., knows AI will probably upend the global economy. He suspects it might even come for his job one day. A few weeks ago, he drove past a data center in Iowa and found the sight unnerving: a “strange, eerie” place, he said, that produced a constant humming sound.

items.title: AI Operating Model: How to Structure Teams and Ownership | Tommaso Maria Ricci
items.snippet: Two tests tell you whether the table is real. First, each decision has one decid...
items.raw_snippet:
Two tests tell you whether the table is real. First, each decision has one decider, not a committee. Second, the people named have seen the table and agreed to it. A table that lives only in a consultant's document changes nothing.

## Funding and prioritization: run a portfolio, not a project list

How AI is funded shapes behavior more than any organization chart. Three funding patterns are common, and each produces a predictable result. [...] An AI operating model is the way a company organizes ownership, structure, funding, talent, governance and delivery for artificial intelligence. It defines which executive is accountable, where AI specialists sit, who pays for platforms and use cases, who approves or stops an initiative and how an idea moves from intake to a system in production. It sits between the AI strategy, which sets priorities, and the daily execution of teams. [...] How to read the result:

 16 to 20. You have an operating model. Focus on scaling and on reviewing the structure once a year.
 10 to 15. The foundations exist, with gaps. The lowest scores usually cluster in funding and in production ownership. Fix those first.
 5 to 9. You have projects, not a model. Start with statements 1, 2 and 3 before approving anything new.
 0 to 4. AI in your company is happening by accident. The 90-day plan below is written for you.
